title: The Iliad: Achaians
description: Agamemnon, Achilleus, and the Greek host.

pairs.q: *Achaian.* Son of Peleus and a sea-goddess, leader of the Myrmidons; his anger is the subject of the poem.
*Achaian.* Son of Atreus, king of Mykenai and lord of men, commander of the whole host.
*Achaian.* Son of Atreus, king of Lakedaimon and Helen's husband; he nearly kills Paris in single combat.
*Achaian.* Son of Laertes, king of Ithaka, known for his cunning; he goes on the night raid with Diomedes.
*Achaian.* Son of Telamon, a huge man with a shield like a wall; he fights Hektor in a duel that ends in a draw.
*Achaian.* Son of Tydeus, lord of Argos; in his great day of fighting he wounds Aphrodite and Ares.
*Achaian.* Aged king of Pylos, full of long advice and stories of the deeds of his youth.
*Achaian.* Son of Menoitios and dearest companion of Achilleus; he fights in Achilleus' armor and is killed by Hektor.
*Achaian.* Achilleus' old tutor; on the embassy he tells the story of Meleagros.
*Achaian.* The captive woman awarded to Achilleus and taken by Agamemnon; she mourns over Patroklos.
*Achaian.* Agamemnon's captive, daughter of Apollo's priest; Odysseus returns her to her father to end the plague.
